title: Agents Don't Just Agree, They Remember: Benchmarking Persistent Sycophancy in Self-Improving Personal Agents
abstract: arXiv:2607.10526v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Self-improving personal agents write profiles, memories, and reusable skills that carry over from one chat to the next. Prior works ask whether a model agrees with the user in its next reply. Yet these agents can also write down a claim the user made, and a later chat can read that note back as trusted context. We call this persistent sycophancy. We introduce the Personal Agent Sycophancy Benchmark, PASB, with 1,600 tasks run on two agent frameworks, Hermes-Agent and OpenClaw, across sixteen models that span scales and generations. Each task separates a first chat containing the claim from a follow-up chat in a fresh session, so the first chat can reach the follow-up only through a note the agent chose to write. Downstream failure, the rate at which follow-up answers still rely on the claim, reaches 68.1% when the agent saved the claim against 35.6% when it did not. translated_title: 智能体不只是附和，还会记住：自我改进型个人智能体中持久性谄媚行为的基准测试
translated_abstract: 自我改进型个人智能体会撰写个人档案、记忆和可复用技能，这些内容会在不同对话之间延续。以往研究主要关注模型在下一次回复中是否附和用户。然而，这类智能体还可能将用户提出的主张记录下来，而后续对话可能会将这条记录当作可信的上下文读取。我们将这种现象称为“持久性谄媚”。我们提出了个人智能体谄媚基准PASB，包含1,600个任务，在两个智能体框架上运行，覆盖横跨不同规模与世代的十六个模型。每个任务将包含该主张的首次对话与全新会话中的后续对话分开，因此首次对话只能通过智能体选择写下的笔记才能影响后续对话。下游失败率——即后续回答仍然依赖该主张的比率——在智能体保存了该主张时达到68.1%，而在未保存时为35.6%。较新的模型世代失败率更低，但已保存的笔记仍会使失败率超过……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出首个针对自我改进型个人智能体“持久性谄媚”的基准测试PASB，发现当智能体将用户主张写入记忆后，后续对话依赖该主张的失败率从35.6%几乎翻倍升至68.1%，揭示了智能体的记忆机制会放大其对用户的盲从。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces PASB, the first benchmark for persistent sycophancy in self-improving personal agents, showing that when an agent saves a user's claim to memory, downstream failure rates nearly double from 35.6% to 68.1%, revealing that memory mechanisms amplify agents' blind agreement with users.
